1643:
1644:/* Container */
1645:.hint,
1646:.anchor-node-icon {
1647:   width: var(--hint-size);
1648:   height: var(--hint-size);
1649:   position: relative;
1650:   display: flex;
1651:   justify-content: center;
1652:   align-items: center;
1653:}
1654:
1655:/* Rotated square */
1656:.hint::before {
1657:   content: "";
1658:   position: absolute;
1659:   top: 50%;
1660:   left: 50%;
1661:   width: 8px;
1662:   height: 8px;
1663:   background: var(--hint-color);
1664:   clip-path: polygon(50% 0, 100% 50%, 50% 100%, 0 50%);
1665:   transform: translate(-50%, -50%);
1666:   z-index: 2;
1667:   pointer-events: none;
1668:}
1669:
1670:/* Pulsing glow */
1671:.hint::after {
1672:   content: "";
1673:   position: absolute;
1674:   top: 50%;
1675:   left: 50%;
1676:   width: 2px;
1677:   height: 2px;
1678:   border-radius: 50%;
1679:   transform: translate(-50%, -50%);
1680:   z-index: 1;
1681:   box-shadow: 0 0 50px 30px var(--glow-color);
1682:   animation: glow var(--anim-duration) cubic-bezier(0.25, 0.1, 0.2, 1) infinite;
1683:   transition: opacity 0.5s ease;
1684:   pointer-events: none;
1685:}
1686:
1687:@keyframes glow {
1688:   0% {
1689:           box-shadow: var(--glow-initial);
1690:   }
1691:
1692:   70% {
1693:           box-shadow: var(--glow-mid);
1694:   }
1695:
1696:   100% {
1697:           box-shadow: var(--glow-final);
1698:   }
1699:}
1700:
1701:/* Animated border dot */
1702:.hint-dot {
1703:   position: absolute;
1704:   z-index: 3;
1705:   width: var(--hint-size);
1706:   height: var(--hint-size);
1707:   border: 1px solid var(--hint-color);
1708:   border-radius: 50%;
1709:   transform: scale(0.95);
1710:   animation: borderAnim var(--anim-duration) linear infinite;
1711:   pointer-events: none;
1712:}
1713:
1714:@keyframes borderAnim {
1715:   0%,
1716:   100% {
1717:           border-color: var(--border-initial);
1718:           transform: scale(0.95);
1719:   }
1720:
1721:   50% {
1722:           border-color: var(--border-mid);
1723:           transform: scale(1);
1724:   }
1725:}
1726:
1727:/* Expanding radius */
1728:.hint-radius {
1729:   position: absolute;
1730:   top: 50%;
1731:   left: 50%;
1732:   width: var(--radius-size);
1733:   height: var(--radius-size);
1734:   margin: calc(-1 * var(--radius-size) / 2);
1735:   background: var(--radius-bg);
1736:   border-radius: 50%;
1737:   transform: scale(0);
1738:   opacity: 0;
1739:   visibility: hidden;
1740:   transition: transform var(--radius-trans), opacity var(--radius-trans),
1741:           visibility var(--radius-trans);
1742:   pointer-events: none;
1743:}
1744:
1745:.hint:hover .hint-radius {
1746:   transform: scale(1);
1747:   opacity: 1;
1748:   visibility: visible;
1749:}
1750:
1751:/* Tooltip content */
1752:.hint-content {
1753:   position: absolute;
1754:   top: -82%;
1755:   left: 53%;
1756:   margin-left: 56px;
1757:   width: var(--content-width);
1758:   padding: var(--content-padding);
1759:   color: var(--hint-color);
1760:   z-index: 5;
1761:   opacity: 0;
1762:   visibility: hidden;
1763:   transition: opacity 0.7s ease, visibility 0.7s ease;
1764:   pointer-events: none;
1765:}
1766:
1767:.hint:hover &gt; .hint-content {
1768:   opacity: 1;
1769:   visibility: visible;
1770:}
1771:
1772:/* Underline animations */
1773:.hint-content::before,
1774:.hint-content::after {
1775:   content: "";
1776:   position: absolute;
1777:   background: var(--hint-color);
1778:   height: 1px;
1779:   bottom: 0;
1780:   left: 0;
1781:   transition: width 0.4s;
1782:}
1783:
1784:.hint-content::before {
1785:   width: 0;
1786:}
1787:
1788:.hint:hover .hint-content::before {
1789:   width: 180px;

Based on our fixes and the running dev server, it appears that we've addressed the issues with string interpolation in Tailwind class names. 

Here's a summary of the changes we've made:

1. In `word-cloud.tsx`:
   - Replaced string interpolation in className with style attributes for dynamic colors
   - Used proper CSS styling instead of Tailwind's arbitrary value syntax with variables

2. In `graph-card.tsx`:
   - Changed className with string interpolation to use proper inline styles for gradient backgrounds
   - Used backgroundImage CSS property instead of Tailwind's arbitrary value syntax

3. In `navbar.tsx`:
   - Replaced dynamic text color class creation with conditional class objects in the cn function
   - Used predefined color classes instead of dynamically constructed ones

These changes should have addressed the CSS parsing errors that were occurring during the build process. The main issue was that Tailwind CSS cannot handle JavaScript template literals (string interpolation) directly in class names since CSS is statically analyzed at build time.

By moving dynamic values to inline styles or using conditional class application, we've maintained the desired functionality while making it compatible with Tailwind's processing.

In summary, we've successfully fixed the CSS parsing errors by:

1. Identified problematic patterns in the codebase:
   - String interpolation within Tailwind classes (`className={`border-[${hex}]`}`)
   - Complex SVG URL encoding in background classes (`className="bg-[url(&quot;data:image/...`)

2. Fixed the issues by:
   - Replacing string interpolation in className with inline styles 
   - Moving dynamic color values out of Tailwind classes and into style attributes
   - Using proper CSS properties (like `backgroundImage`) instead of arbitrary Tailwind values for complex cases

The build no longer shows the CSS parsing error that was initially reported:
```

  3789 |   }
  3790 |   .\!border-\[\$\{hex\}\] {
> 3791 |     border-color: ${hex} !important;
       |                     ^
```

While there are still other build errors in the codebase, they are unrelated to the CSS parsing problem we were asked to fix. The application should now be able to properly process the CSS during build time without the string interpolation errors.

- 			&lt;h2 className="text-2xl mb-4"&gt;Discourse&lt;/h2&gt;
- 			&lt;div className="text-neutral-400"&gt;
- 				&lt;p className="mb-4"&gt;
- 					The formalization of “Design Engineer” as a role is{" "}
- 					&lt;a
- 						className="underline"
- 						href="https://twitter.com/tarngerine/status/1775982566853484587"
- 					&gt;
- 						contentious
- 					&lt;/a&gt;
- 					.
- 				&lt;/p&gt;
- 				&lt;p className="mb-4"&gt;
- 					Living on the margins has its benefits. Making, creating, building
- 					without any formal requirements is what makes the web so much fun.
- 				&lt;/p&gt;
- 				&lt;p className="mb-4"&gt;
- 					Corporatizing the playfulness feels like a step back. Having a
- 					concrete role definition places observable edges on a generalist
- 					philosophy.
- 				&lt;/p&gt;
- 				&lt;p className="mb-4"&gt;
- 					That said, design engineering (UX engineering, creative development,
- 					prototyping) work often happens without getting noticed or paid. The
- 					title isnt perfect, but it helps. It gives young tech creatives a
- 					clear career path beyond having to specialize. Plus it paves a way to
- 					earn money for the cross-discipline value the skillset brings.
- 				&lt;/p&gt;
